newsitem.title: UK: Urals crude begins its winter rally now Iraq gone.
newsitem.headline: Urals crude begins its winter rally now Iraq gone.

text.p: Russia's benchmark export crude oil, Urals, may have begun its traditional winter rally, supported by worsening loading delays in Novorossiisk, strong high sulphur fuel oil prices and the receding prospect of Iraqi crude exports, Mediterranean crude traders said on Wednesday.
In both 1994 and 1995, Urals crude delivered in the Mediterranean reached a premium to benchmark Dated Brent, against a 1995 average discount of 41 cents.
"The sellers have the bit between their teeth with the prospect of higher prices," said German crude trader.
"We are talking about Urals rising to parity to Dated Brent, because in winter you do get to those sort of levels. Not all in one move perhaps, but we will get there," he added.
From a $1.03 discount to Dated Brent one week ago, Urals has already jumped 20 cents and dealers say this could be the beginning of its winter rally.
"I think much will depend on the weather, but the differential to Dated will definitely narrow," said a major Italian refiner.

Bad weather has already begun to disrupt loadings from Russia's main crude export terminal of Novorossiisk on the Black Sea. And the September loading schedule have been further disrupted by maintenance on the crude pipelines feeding the port.
Demand from Mediterranean refiners is already pushing Urals prices up as strong high sulphur fuel oil prices bolster the sour crude refining margin.
In turn, high sulphur fuel oil is expected to stay strong as Russian exports experience their seasonal decline in winter to cater for rising inland demand.

It is not clear whether Russia will impose a ban on exports this winter, as they have in recent years, but exports are expected to fall anyway due to high domestic prices and a possible increase in export tariffs.
